key_insight: FiLIP trains CT representations using report-derived abnormal findings, avoiding the assumption that different patient cases should always be pushed apart.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support CT finding recognition and radiology report generation, but clinical utility remains unestablished.
method: Use a large language model to extract abnormal finding phrases from radiology reports.
Encode those findings with a biomedical text embedding model to construct target representations.
Train a CT image encoder to predict these finding-based representations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports better multi-label zero-shot finding classification than weakly supervised approaches in in-domain and external-domain evaluations, plus benefits for fine-tuned report generation, without numerical results.
watch_item: Errors or omissions in report-derived findings could propagate into training targets; the abstract does not describe extraction validation.
paper_title: Findings-aware Language-Image Pretraining for CT Volume Interpretation
